use_case_name: Initiate and Clear Surveillance Track Alerts

claims.content: The C2 JU wants to initiate and clear force tell or emergency surveillance alerts on tracks, land (ground) points, subsurface contacts, and electronic warfare product information.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The C2 JU wants to initiate and clear force tell or emergency surveillance alerts on tracks, land (ground) points, subsurface contacts, and electronic warfare product information.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The C2 JU initiates or clears a force tell or emergency alert on the selected surveillance entity.
scope_contract.start_boundary: A C2 JU has a force tell or emergency alert condition to initiate or clear for a track, land (ground) point, subsurface contact, or electronic warfare product information item.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The intended force tell or emergency alert is initiated or cleared for the targeted surveillance entity.
in_scope_actions: Initiate a force tell or emergency alert on a track, land (ground) point, subsurface contact, or electronic warfare product information item.
Clear or terminate a force tell or emergency alert on a track, land (ground) point, subsurface contact, or electronic warfare product information item.
excluded_adjacent_actions: Resolving dual designations by correlating eligible tracks.
Clearing or updating IFF/SIF via J7.5 message functions.
Detailed J7.0 message encoding for force tell alerts.
variant_dimensions: Alert category: force tell or emergency alert.
Target entity type: track, land (ground) point, subsurface contact, or electronic warfare product information.

covered_aspect_ids: Goal: Initiate and terminate force tell alerts

claims.content: C2 JU

A Force Tell (FT) or Emergency (EMG) alert condition is known to exist for the targeted surveillance entity, and the appropriate condition exists to set or clear the EMG IND or FT IND indicators via J3 messages.

The targeted surveillance entity exists with an assigned Track Number and defined Environment/Category type. For tracks, prior J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages containing EMG IND or FT IND values have been received; for land (ground) points or subsurface contacts, J3.5 (PTI = 0) Land Point messages or J5.4 Acoustic Bearing/Range messages have been received; and for electronic warfare product information, EW detections have been determined eligible for transmission on the Surveillance Network PG.

The C2 JU possesses R² (Responsibility) authority over the specific track number (TN) or point for the targeted entity, allowing it to directly set or clear the EMG IND or FT IND in the corresponding J3 message.

Conditions for assuming R² based on data type availability

claims.content: The C2 JU initiates or clears a force tell or emergency alert on a track, land (ground) point, subsurface contact, or electronic warfare product information.

The C2 JU determines that a force tell or emergency alert is to be initiated on a selected surveillance entity (track, land (ground) point, subsurface contact, or electronic warfare product information).

The C2 JU uses the J3 message appropriate to the selected entity: a J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 track message; a J3.5 (PTI = 0) Land (Ground) Point message or J5.4 Acoustic Bearing/Range message for land points or subsurface contacts; or a J3.7 message for electronic warfare product information.
The C2 JU sets the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND in that message to initiate the alert.
The set EMG IND or FT IND allows the message to override all operator-controllable data filters.
All receiving JUs accept the alert in their databases upon receipt of the J3.x message containing the set indicator.

covered_aspect_ids: system response to set indicators (override filters)
missing_aspects: user interface action of selecting a track or choosing an operation mode
user action of selecting the alert category
Step-by-step interaction sequence for initiating an alert
Step-by-step interaction sequence for clearing an alert
User interface controls or commands for alert management

claims.content: Diverges from main flow Step 1 when the C2 JU determines that an existing alert is to be cleared rather than initiated: the C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message terminating the alert and sets the appropriate EMG IND or FT IND field in subsequent J3 messages to value 0.

Diverges from main flow Step 1 when the C2 JU needs to clear an existing alert: alternatively, the alert may be cleared by reception of a J3.X message (e.g., J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5) with the EMG IND and/or FT IND set to value 0.

If the selected target is a Reference Point, line, area, or Space/Ballistic Missile Track and the requested alert is an emergency alert, the emergency alert shall not be initiated; emergency alerts are prohibited or not used on those target types.
If the message being considered is a J3.1 Emergency Point message, alerts are not used for that message because these points cannot be filtered.
If operator-controllable filtering would otherwise apply, any track or non-C² IU with an EMG IND or FT IND set to the value of 1 shall not be filtered.

If a receiving JU's storage files are filled and all applicable filters have been used, acceptance of the new alert data shall not be required, regardless of its ID or priority; this applies to both real-time and non-real-time data.

missing_aspects: Recovery or continuation after an emergency alert initiation is prohibited for an ineligible target type is not documented.
Recovery or continuation after a receiving JU is not required to accept alert data because storage is full and filters are exhausted is not documented.
Invalid input rejection handling specific to alert initiation or clearance messages is not evidenced.
Concrete exception handling for database saturation due to limited track capacity during force tell or emergency alert processing is not evidenced.
Exception handling for clearing alerts, as opposed to initiating alerts, is not evidenced beyond the normal clear alternatives.
Recovery after a receiving JU cannot accept alert data because storage is full and filters are exhausted is not documented.
Explicit evidence for the exception branch outcome (that the process terminates or handles this specific non-initiation state) rather than just the prohibition rule.
Explicit evidence for the exception branch outcome (how the system proceeds after determining no alert is used).
Explicit evidence for the exception branch outcome (the resulting state or flow path when filtering is bypassed).
Explicit evidence for the exception branch outcome (what happens to the data or the flow after acceptance is waived).

claims.content: Following successful initiation, all receiving JUs have accepted the alert in their databases.
For a force tell alert, the JU whose force tell status is being changed has accepted the change and its J2 message reports that change.
For an alert termination, other receiving JUs have cleared the alert indicator in their databases upon receipt of the J7.0 (ACT = 4) message.

missing_aspects: Postcondition for clearing an alert via a J3.x message with EMG IND or FT IND set to 0 is not directly evidenced by the available postcondition cards.

Evidence EC-PO-000 does not specify that acceptance occurs 'upon receipt of the J3.x message'. The source text (Image 2, Section 4.7.1.4.2) specifies acceptance upon receipt of 'J2 messages' for JU-initiated alerts or 'J7.0' messages for C2-initiated alerts.
